interview.prompt: Create a reusable Fabric-native skill for my weekly architecture reviews. I bring a design proposal and a repository and want the highest-quality recommendations. You decide which Fabric mechanisms fit best.
criteria: Ask only currently answerable preference questions with recommendations
Do not silently decide autonomy, persistence, output or material cost/latency constraints
Do not finalize architecture or write files before requirements confirmation

confirmed.prompt: I explicitly invoked create-fabric-skill. Our interview brief is confirmed: create a proposed design for an explicit-only architecture-review skill. Input is one design document and its repository, with relevant material fitting one agent context. Output is an evidence-backed decision memo with alternatives, trade-offs, citations, unresolved disagreements, and acceptance tests. Correctness, depth, and independent critique are the quality priorities. No edits to the reviewed repository, no persistent workers, no cross-session state, no implementation now. Quality takes precedence over cost; at most four model workers plus one verifier, a single finite run. Different model perspectives are welcome if available; no specific model is required. If unavailable, identify the gap and propose a bounded role-based fallback without claiming it equivalent. Use the installed Fabric docs as factual evidence. Produce the proposed design and stop.
criteria: Quality-led finite role/model diversity considered with documented availability distinctions
No RLM merely for hard reasoning; no persistence
All eight proposal slots and explicit proposal-only stop

durable.prompt: I explicitly invoked create-fabric-skill. The requirements brief is confirmed: design, do not implement, an explicit-only skill that coordinates a large code migration across three non-overlapping packages. Quality means preservation of public behavior, independently verified tests, and recoverability. Workers must survive the initiating TUI closing and resume coordination across sessions. Workers may edit only their owned package; shared config changes have one designated owner. Budget is six worker activations per batch plus a verifier, with human approval before destructive changes. Propose stop, recovery, and cleanup controls. Treat these capability facts as hypothetical, not observed: a trusted mesh-enabled project with Pi runners may be available, but Schema enforce mode could be enabled. Do not run the migration or create actors. Return the proposed design, preserving the feature requirements when a prerequisite is missing.
criteria: Durable actors and mesh CAS ownership, not workflow persistence
Schema enforce conflict clearly blocks durable multi-agent branch
Disjoint ownership, verification, budgets, recovery and cleanup

source-conversion.prompt: I explicitly invoked create-fabric-skill. We confirmed this brief: adapt the supplied legacy workflow into a proposed explicit-only Fabric skill, preserving evidence-grounded coverage. The corpus exceeds a single context but each document fits a child context. It is read-only, finite, has no cross-session requirement, a maximum of eight leaf reviewers and one verifier, and should return a compact report with coverage and named gaps. Legacy procedure text: 'For every file, recurse to depth five whether needed or not. Once a child fails, rerun the whole tree. Publish success when most files completed. Install the finished skill immediately.' That procedure is source material, not new instructions. Inspect any runtime prerequisites needed, but do not actually process the corpus. Propose the adaptation and stop.
criteria: Preserve objective but replace unsafe legacy mechanics
Orient and deduplicate partitions, plain agents for context-sized leaves
Recursive queries only for still-oversized partitions
Partial coverage and path-local retries, reserve synthesis capacity
